summary: Proposes an ASCII text file of hostnames, related to RFCs 606, 608, 623 and 625.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 627 announces that the NIC's official host-name file is available at OFFICE-1. The ASCII file lists each host's name, address and status, and hosts can fetch updates through FTP.

subtitle: Announcement of the NIC's official ASCII host-name file.

tldr.problem: Network hosts needed a shared source for official host names, addresses and status information.
tldr.mechanism: The NIC maintains the ASCII file HOSTS.TXT at OFFICE-1 and makes it available through FTP; hosts are responsible for fetching updates.
tldr.outcome: The announcement says changes and additions would be made weekly and describes the option to register one official nickname.

today: RFC 627 announces the availability of the NIC-maintained ASCII host-name file and explains how hosts could obtain updates.

sections.title: Where to Find the Host-Name File
sections.content: The official ASCII host-name file defined in RFCs 606 and 608 is available at OFFICE-1, host address 43 decimal, under pathname <NETINFO>HOSTS.TXT. The NIC maintains the file and encourages all hosts to use its names in their monitors.
sections.plainLanguage: The NIC makes the official host-name file available at OFFICE-1. The announcement gives its address and pathname.

sections.title: File Contents and Updates
sections.content: The file currently contains a host name, host address and host status. The NIC hopes to add more attributes. It says changes and additions will be made weekly and that each network host is responsible for accessing the file through FTP to obtain new information.
sections.plainLanguage: The file lists host names, addresses and status. The NIC plans weekly changes, and each host is responsible for fetching new information using FTP.

sections.title: Official Names and Nicknames
sections.content:
The file did not yet include nicknames. A site could register one official nickname, which would be added as received; systems with name-to-address translation were encouraged but not required to use nicknames. The NIC asks hosts to choose official names carefully so that changes and nicknames remain limited.

The RFC invites corrections, additions and comments to the NIC and asks hosts interested in keeping a secondary copy to contact it.
sections.plainLanguage: A site could ask the NIC to add one nickname, but nicknames were optional. The NIC asks sites to choose official names carefully and invites volunteers to keep a secondary copy.
